metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Israel

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Israel using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD/OECD-IEA practice is to use sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each country/economy. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be verified from the provided text. For analysts working with the PISA microdata, the recommended approach is to apply the provided student sampling weights and the corresponding variance estimation method used in the PISA database documentation, and to use the published plausible-value/scaling outputs for achievement and related scales.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The provided factsheet is a descriptive reporting of PISA 2022 creative thinking results and does not document an analysis pipeline that explicitly states how plausible values (PVs) were handled for any student-level predictive model. PV handling is therefore not applicable to the extraction because no ML model or PV-based outcome construction is described in the text excerpt. Missing-data handling is not reported in the factsheet excerpt because it focuses on summary statistics and cross-country comparisons rather than methodological details of imputation/deletion procedures.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for Israel is described as 6,251 students in 193 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 132,500 15-year-olds in Israel. The factsheet does not provide additional inclusion/exclusion rules beyond this description (e.g., no further task/module completion filters are stated in the excerpt), so the extraction uses the stated Israel assessment-completer sample for the PISA 2022 creative thinking reporting.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet reports descriptive results for Israel on the PISA Creative Thinking cognitive test administered to 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment measures three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. For Israel, students’ mean creative thinking score is 32 on a 60-point scale, which is on par with the OECD average (33). The factsheet also reports proficiency distribution (75% at least Level 3; 30% at Level 5 or 6) and relationships with mathematics and reading performance (correlations of 0.76 and 0.74, respectively; 32% of creative thinking variance uniquely attributed to mathematics performance). It further highlights within-Israel gaps by socio-economic status and gender, and reports associations between creative thinking and students’ beliefs/attitudes and school environment indicators. Methodological details on PV handling, missing data, and weighting are not provided in the excerpt, and the reported relationships are descriptive rather than causal.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking results rather than an empirical ML study. As such, it does not specify a predictive modeling design, algorithmic pipeline, or target-variable ML evaluation metrics, so fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty. The extraction therefore focuses on the assessment design and reported descriptive benchmarks (means, proficiency levels, and reported associations) without fabricating methodological details that are not present in the provided text.
